title: "Open Source Software Development Track"
description: "NYC Open Data Lab Summer Internship"
---

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Overview

The Open Source Software Development Track is designed for an intern interested in building public, reusable tools that make civic open data easier to access, analyze, and teach with.

The intern will contribute to the NYC Open Data Lab by developing R packages modeled after `nycOpenData`, with the goal of expanding access to open data from cities beyond New York City.

## Mission

The mission of this track is to help create a growing ecosystem of open-source R packages that make municipal open data more accessible to students, researchers, educators, journalists, analysts, and the broader public.

Rather than completing isolated assignments, the intern will produce public-facing software that can be used, cited, improved, and shared beyond the internship.

## Primary Responsibilities

The intern will work on developing R packages that provide convenient access to public open data APIs. Responsibilities may include:

- Exploring municipal open data portals

- Identifying useful API endpoints

- Writing R functions to access datasets

- Cleaning and standardizing returned data

- Writing documentation and examples

- Creating package vignettes

- Building package websites using `pkgdown`

- Writing tests

- Using GitHub for version control and issue tracking

- Preparing packages for public release

## Expected Deliverables

By the end of the summer, the intern should aim to produce:

- One or more public R package repositories

- Documented package functions

- Example use cases or vignettes

- A package website

- A short final reflection or technical blog post

- A final presentation/demo of the completed work

The exact number of packages will depend on the complexity of each city’s open data portal and API structure. Quality, documentation, and usability are prioritized over quantity.

## Professional Development Goals

Through this track, the intern will gain experience with:

- R package development

- API access and data retrieval

- Reproducible workflows

- Git and GitHub

- Open-source collaboration

- Technical writing

- Public software documentation

- Civic technology and open data

The goal is for the intern to leave with meaningful public work that can be included in a portfolio, resume, graduate school application, or future job application.

## Mentorship and Expectations

The intern will meet regularly with the NYC Open Data Lab director to review progress, troubleshoot issues, and plan next steps.

The intern is expected to:

- Communicate progress consistently

- Ask questions when blocked

- Document work clearly

- Commit code regularly

- Prioritize reproducibility and usability

- Treat the project as a public contribution

## End-of-Summer Outcome

By the end of the internship, the intern should have contributed to the broader open data community by creating tools that help people more easily access and work with public data.

The ideal outcome is not only a completed package, but a reusable development workflow that future interns and contributors can build upon.
